findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on any I/O error (missing file, permissions, etc.)
findings.failure_mode: Untrusted or missing file input aborts the entire process instead of returning a typed error
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, IoError>. Use fs::read_to_string(path).map_err(...) and propagate with ?

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on both missing field and invalid integer string
findings.failure_mode: A malformed CSV line (missing second field or non-numeric value) panics instead of yielding a typed parse/missing-field error
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') to extract fields, check .is_some() for the second field, use .parse::<u16>().map_err(...) for the numeric conversion, and return a typed error

findings.problem: Lossy as cast: u32 -> u16 via .parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16
findings.failure_mode: A valid u32 value greater than u16::MAX silently truncates, producing incorrect domain data
findings.fix: Parse directly as u16 via .parse::<u16>() or use u16::try_from(value).map_err(...) to reject out-of-range values with a typed error

findings.problem: Uses line.split(',').map(...).collect() then accesses parts[0] and parts[1] by unchecked index
findings.failure_mode: split + collect allocates a full Vec for every line, then parts[0] and parts[1] are unchecked indexing — either index may panic on short lines
findings.fix: Replace with split_once(',') to extract the first delimiter-only pair, then .map(|(name, val)| ...) without collect or indexing

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) — side-effecting I/O inside what should be the pure parsing layer
findings.failure_mode: Logging inside the data-loading core couples it to std::io, making it untestable in isolation and producing unwanted stdout in consumer processes
findings.fix: Remove println! from the pure core. If logging is needed, let the imperative shell (caller) log after the function returns, or accept a callback/handler abstraction

findings.problem: The function mixes I/O (fs::read_to_string, println!) with data parsing in a single monolithic function
findings.failure_mode: Cannot unit-test the parsing logic in isolation; every test requires filesystem access and handles I/O errors that are not part of the domain contract
findings.fix: Split into two functions: (1) parse_records(line: &str) -> Result<Record, ParseError> — pure and testable, (2) load_jobs(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, JobError> — shell that handles I/O and delegates to (1)

findings.problem: Allocates Vec<String> per line for split parts when only two fields are needed
findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary heap allocation per line degrades throughput; split_once + &str avoids all per-field allocations
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') and work with &str slices throughout the parsing pipeline; only allocate String in the final Record if the API requires owned data

findings.problem: No benchmark, profiler, or allocation evidence exists for this I/O-bound function
findings.failure_mode: Cannot verify whether this implementation meets throughput/latency requirements; no baseline for regression testing
findings.fix: Add a criterion or similar benchmark measuring parse-throughput on representative input, and an allocation audit (e.g., dhat, or manual tracking) for the hot path

findings.problem: No [dev-dependencies], [[bench]], or [profile] sections — no bench.toml/criterion section, no overflow-check or panic-strategy configuration
findings.failure_mode: No instrumentation hooks (overflow checks, debug assertions, allocation tracking) can be enabled via Cargo.toml
findings.fix: Add criterion or similar bench dependency, overflow-checks = true in profile.release, and any needed dev-dependencies

no profiler evidence (flamegraph, perf, dhat) for allocation patterns
no allocation audit for the per-line Vec<String> allocation in the hot path

residual_risk: Static review identified 7 blockers and 3 warnings across Holzman Rust constraints: forbidden constructs (unwrap, as cast, unchecked indexing), functional core violations (hidden I/O, mixed concerns), and allocation anti-patterns. No commands were executed and no tests exist in the crate. Full repair requires implementing typed error returns, split_once-based parsing, direct u16 parsing, removing println! from the core, splitting into pure/impure layers, and adding a test suite with behavior tests.
